text: Up in the attic, the violin sat in its case, like it was holding its breath. Dust was fuzzy on the latches. Light came in through a cracked window, thin and like something from the Bible, moving dust around. It just floated and landed, no rush. The roof timbers went creaking from the heat. Wasps had built a gray paper city under the eaves. At some point, someone rosined the bow until it shined. Now the horsehair hangs loose. Loose like an old thought. The strings were tuned to nothing. But they hummed faintly when the house moved. Not really music, more like memory. Chalk marks on the floor from a child had a scale. Fading into gray. Next to them, music paper curled up like a dried leaf. Notes unread. Nobody came to open the case. Afternoon got deeper. Rain started, drumming softly on the shingles. The violin waited. Patience of things you love then put down. At dusk, one string loosened from the damp. Sighed once against the wood, then quiet. Somewhere below, a door closed. Softly.
